name: Gloria Pruitt

five_sec.what_is_it: Some kind of supper-planning thing, 'Less Stress, More Dinners'
five_sec.who_for: Young mamas with little ones, from the picture
five_sec.trust_why: It don't say what it costs or who's behind it up top
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Pictures of food in circles around a phone; I reckon they might send it

full_page.what_stopped_me: 'Try Free for 14 Days' - those are the exact words that got my daughter charged a whole year. No price on it neither. I did like that it says you can shop yourself at the store of your choice, and there's a Diabetic plan
full_page.whats_missing: A price, 'no card' said plain, a phone number

EM.quote: That young'un read me 'Try Free for 14 Days' and I said stop right there, honey. That's how your aunt got charged a whole year.

five_sec.what_is_it: A recipe and list program for the phone
five_sec.trust_why: 'Free Trial' right there in the middle, even if it says no card
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Says recipes and grocery lists, all in one app

full_page.what_stopped_me: After the trial it's $5.95 a month or $49 a year. I write my list on paper for nothing

PTE.quote: 'Free Trial, no card required.' Then what? Then it's $5.95 a month, that's what. I write my list on the back of an envelope for free.

five_sec.what_is_it: A phone thing that tells you what's for supper
five_sec.trust_why: My granddaughter says it's AI. I don't trust a computer to feed Earl
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Little messages on the phone saying 'Tonight's dinner is a good one'

full_page.what_stopped_me: Twenty-five dollars a month, and one that's a hundred

OL.quote: A hundred dollars a month for the 'Always-On' one. I reckon Earl's disability check would laugh at that.

five_sec.what_is_it: Boxes of food they mail to you
five_sec.delivers_food_why: HelloFresh boxes right in the middle of the screen

full_page.what_stopped_me: Mail-order food 35 minutes from a Walmart, with a subscription in the fine print

HF.quote: Open a box to reveal your offer. Honey, I've been to the county fair. I know how that game works.

five_sec.what_is_it: Something that plans the week's suppers and texts the family
five_sec.who_for: Families where everybody's got a phone
five_sec.trust_why: Says 'no card needed' plain as day, which I like, but I don't know what Instacart is
five_sec.next_step: Ask my daughter if it's safe
five_sec.delivers_food_why: My granddaughter read it: 'We don't deliver food'

full_page.what_stopped_me: It's all about putting groceries in a cart on the phone. I go to Walmart once a month with cash and a paper list, and it don't say what I do instead. Then there's '14 days free', which sounds like a trial to me. Long page, lots of little grey writing, no phone number
full_page.whats_missing: A way to just print the list, a phone number, big-pot plain suppers, diabetic choices up top (my granddaughter found 'Diabetic-friendly dinners' way down at the bottom)

DD.quote: It says plain 'no card needed' and a lady named Sarah made it. That's something. But I don't buy groceries on the phone, and it don't say what I do instead.

dd_offer.why: 'Free forever' and then '14 days free' - which is it? Sounds like one of them trials
dd_offer.expect_day_15: I reckon on day 15 they'll start wanting money, or ask for a card.

head_to_head.reason: Only one that says free forever and no card, with a real lady's name on it. I'd still have my daughter look first

EM.reason: eMeals won't say what it costs and says 'free trial'

PTE.reason: Plan to Eat costs money after two weeks

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page, top of the screen in big type: 'No card. No charge. Shop online or print the list for your Walmart trip', with Sarah's picture and a way to call or write her.
